content:
Not all chargers are created equal. Some of the most impressive designs I've ever seen come equipped with in-car displays, the ability to charge two MacBooks simultaneously, RGB lighting effects, and a pair of windows on the metal casing that let you peek into the inner workings — Sharge's brand-new Shargeek 300 charger is seriously impressive, and during its launch promotion, you should at least go take a look. Here are some of my hands-on experiences.

Sharge Shargeek 300 Charger Review

The brand-new Sharge Shargeek 300 charger is built from solid metal, packs a 24,000mAh battery capacity, and can deliver up to 300W of power to your devices. The translucent design, RGB lighting effects, and built-in display are among its highlights, and it's currently available on Amazon at a launch promotion price of US$199.

Features at a glance:

  • 300W total output — charge 2 laptops + 1 smartphone simultaneously
  • CNC aluminium alloy housing with advanced thermal management
  • 24,000mAh battery capacity — fully compliant with airline regulations
  • Equipped with dual USB-C, USB-A, and adjustable DC output (5V–28V)
  • Provides stable power for Starlink, portable fridges, soldering irons, camera monitors, LED film lights, and other DC-powered devices
  • 140W USB-C input — the Shargeek 300 goes from 0% to 100% in just 44 minutes
  • Full-tab cell technology — operating temperature reduced by up to 35%
  • 1.9-inch smart display with Sentinel BMS — real-time charge and discharge power curves, individual cell voltages, cycle counts, usage history, and estimated remaining usage time

9to5Toys take

Sharge is an underrated brand. The charging devices they produce are among the most eye-catching on the market, and the brand-new Shargeek 300 charger is absolutely the best example.

This thing is absolutely stunning. Not everyone likes this cyberpunk-style transparent aesthetic that exposes the inner workings, paired with RGB lighting and a built-in display, but I absolutely love it, and I'm willing to bet you'll fall for it once you hold it in your hands.

What you're looking at is a unibody chassis made from CNC-machined metal — most chargers on the market that come with displays use plastic casings... I really hate that approach, but I absolutely love Sharge's design. This thing is built like a tank.

Based on what I've seen, this thing looks absolutely incredible — so good that I'll definitely be putting it on display in my office as a decorative piece.

This brand's products have never let me down, never had any issues, and honestly, if you haven't noticed them yet, they're absolutely worth keeping an eye on. That has been the case throughout the roughly past month of testing this brand-new Shargeek 300W charger.

Speaking of output power distribution, there's a total of 300W. When all three USB ports are used simultaneously, the two main USB-C ports can each output 140W, while the traditional USB-A provides an additional 20W. Based on what I've seen, it's more than enough to charge three devices at once, because when I'm out and about, I rarely need more than a device or two.

Sharge says that when charging via USB-C1 or USB-C2 on its own, it can take your MacBook Pro from 0% to 50% in roughly 25 to 30 minutes. The results from my testing matched up perfectly — my 14-inch Pro went from nearly dead to just over 50% in 27 minutes.

Alright, let's talk about this display. I absolutely love the feel of it — there's a nostalgic yet ultra-modern vibe to it, and I'm a huge fan.

In terms of functionality, it basically shows you everything you need to know, plus a whole lot of stuff you don't really need to know — real-time charging status, discharge power curves that I don't particularly care about but love looking at, individual cell voltages, cycle counts, usage history, and various other data. From what I've seen, everything works really well, and more importantly, every time I pull it out to use it, it gives me a feeling of being in Blade Runner or Cyberpunk 2077.

For enthusiasts and true professional users, the charging and voltage analytics data can be put to excellent use — this is the most comprehensive power data I've ever seen on a consumer-grade charger.

Well, I've found my new favourite charger. It performs just as well as it looks, and it will remain on my daily gear list for the foreseeable future.
